prize_parts.citation: For a body of work that renews lyric, narrative and essay through hybrid forms, and reads antiquity through modern desire and grief.

statement.case_for: Carson has an unmistakable voice that holds across verse-novel, elegy, essay and drama. Autobiography of Red recasts the Geryon myth as a modern verse novel. Nox makes grief and the limits of translation into a form that cannot be separated from its material shape. The formal invention is not decoration. It comes from a long engagement with Greek and Latin literature, so the intellectual depth does not depend on novelty. She writes in English, so the linguistic achievement can be assessed without a translator in between, which is not the case for several other candidates. The work has been sustained over decades without settling into one manner. I have reread my opening view against my colleagues' arguments and I still place her first on voice, formal and linguistic achievement, and imaginative depth. This rests on public knowledge of the work and not on a fresh reading of the corpus.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is scope and sustained quality. Much of her standing rests on a few landmark books, and a large share of her output is translation, scholarship, performance text or book-object work. It is hard to weigh that against an original literary oeuvre, and its effect often depends on physical format. If the committee cannot define the citation narrowly enough, the award risks honoring a method or a hybrid category more than a body of literary work. Cărtărescu offers a more conventionally legible kind of sustained achievement, a large, internally coherent architecture of long prose. I find that case serious.

responses.point: Mattson ranks Cărtărescu first for a visionary, patterned prose voice in which memory, the body and metaphysical speculation form a large imaginative architecture. She asks whether Carson's hybrid forms add up to sustained quality across the whole corpus.
responses.response: I accept the point about scale and coherence. Cărtărescu's voice is as distinctive as Carson's, and a comparison on those criteria alone is close. We differ on range versus depth of a single mode. Carson has changed her instruments across verse-novel, elegy, essay and drama, while the Cărtărescu case rests on a recurring set of obsessions on a very large canvas. Your worry about unevenness in Carson is fair, and I cannot dismiss it. My answer is that the citation should rest on the books that carry the achievement and should not claim every occasional or experimental piece. I also remain uncertain how Romanian density survives translation, which is why I keep Cărtărescu as a first alternative and not as a lesser option.

responses.point: Sem-Sandberg values Carson's strongly individual voice and her recasting of Greek material. He says a citation must define its scope carefully because genre labels are contested, and he doubts whether the book-object works count as literature in the sense of Nobel's will.
responses.response: I agree the scope has to be fixed. I would anchor it in the written text, meaning the verse novel, the elegiac and lyric writing, and the essays. Nox would count as a poetic text whose format belongs to its poetics, not as a visual artwork judged by other standards. Under that framing the question of whether hybrid forms qualify is answered by the writing itself. Where I cannot answer is how much weight the later, more format-dependent work should carry. I would not rest the citation on it.

responses.point: Carlberg ranks Carson first and notes that her translations and classical adaptations could blur what is credited as original creation. She also notes that her reputation rests on a few landmark books.
responses.response: I share both reservations and they affect how I would word the citation. The translations show the depth of her engagement with antiquity, but they should be evidence for the original work and not the object of the prize. I would also not claim that every decade shows the same peak. Your point about landmark books is the main challenge to the maturity criterion. I can only answer it by pointing to variety of method over time, and I cannot verify that variety book by book.

responses.point: Olsson ranks Carson first and argues that the hybrid, visual and translation work should be treated as part of the achievement and not as peripheral. He ranks Adonis second for remaking Arabic poetic language.
responses.response: I agree with you on the classical depth, but I would qualify how much the translation work should count. If it becomes part of the credited achievement, the citation widens in the way Carlberg and Sem-Sandberg warn about, so I would keep it as supporting context. On Adonis, I agree that his formal and linguistic achievement is substantial and influential. His significance is clear to me from public critical consensus, but I cannot judge the prosody in translation, and I cannot tell whether the later work matches the formative period. That leaves me less able to defend him on literary merit than I am Carson, and it is the reason I do not name him as an alternative.

uncertainties: My assessment of all candidates rests on public knowledge of representative works, not on a verified reading of full corpora. I have not independently verified any source.

Carson writes in English, so I can judge her linguistic achievement more directly than Cărtărescu's or Can Xue's. That asymmetry may inflate my confidence in her relative to translated writers, and I cannot correct for it from the supplied evidence.
It is unresolved how much weight translation, scholarship, performance and book-object work should carry in a citation for a literary oeuvre.
Whether the reputation of Carson's oeuvre rests on a few landmark books or on a sustained body of work across decades is not settled by the evidence I have.
Romanian, Chinese and Arabic prose and poetry reach me only through translation, so close comparison on voice and linguistic achievement across these candidates is limited.
statement.conflict_note: None apparent from the supplied profile. The profile documents only collegial service with the other committee members and the 2019 renewal round. My own practice as a novelist is context and is not a reason to favor any candidate.
